questions.problem: Given that $X∼B(7,0.7),$ compute $P(X=5).$ Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ where $n$ is the number of trials, and $p$ is the probability of success on each trial,  we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(7,0.7),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x})(0.7)^{x}(0.3)^{7-x}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=5) & =f(5) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{5})(0.7)^{5}(0.3)^{7-5} \\  & =21(0.7)^{5}(0.3)^{2} \\  & ≈0.3177\end{aligned}
$$

to $4$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x})(0.8)^{x}(0.2)^{7-x}.
$$

Computing $P(X<6)$ will require us to compute $f(x)$ at $x=0,1,2,…,5.$ However, if we compute the complement $P(X\ge 6)$ instead, then we will only have to compute $f(x)$ at $x=6,7,$ which will result in a much faster computation.

Computing $P(X\ge 6),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 6) & =P(X\in {6,7}) \\  & =f(6)+f(7) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{6})(0.8)^{6}(0.2)^{7-6}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{7})(0.8)^{7}(0.2)^{7-7} \\  & =7(0.8)^{6}(0.2)+(0.8)^{7} \\  & ≈0.577\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<6) & =1-P(X\ge 6) \\  & ≈1-0.577 \\  & =0.423\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 3) & =1-P(X<3) \\  & ≈1-0.227 \\  & =0.773\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

canonical_examples.problem: Given that $X \sim B(6, 0.7),$ compute $P(X = 2).$ Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X \sim B(n,p),$ where $n$ is the number of trials, and $p$ is the probability of success on each trial,  we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x) =
\displaystyle \binom{n}{x} p^x (1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X \sim B(6, 0.7),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x) =
\displaystyle \binom{6}{x} (0.7)^x (0.3)^{6-x}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=2) & =f(2) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{2})(0.7)^{2}(0.3)^{6-2} \\  & =15(0.7)^{2}(0.3)^{4} \\  & ≈0.0595\end{aligned}
$$

to $4$ decimal places.

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Using the Complement
canonical_examples.problem: Given that $X \sim B(7, 0.2),$ compute $P(X \geq 2).$ Round your final answer to $4$ decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a binomial random variable $X \sim B(n,p),$ we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x) =
\displaystyle \binom{n}{x} p^x (1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X \sim B(7, 0.2),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x) =
\displaystyle \binom{7}{x} (0.2)^x (0.8)^{7-x}.
$$

Computing $P(X \geq 2)$ will require us to compute $f(x)$ at $x=2, 3, 4, \ldots, 7.$ However, if we compute the complement $P(X < 2)$ instead, then we will only have to compute $f(x)$ at $x=0, 1,$ which will result in a much faster computation.

Computing $P(X < 2),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & =P(X\in {0,1}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{0})(0.2)^{0}(0.8)^{7-0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{1})(0.2)^{1}(0.8)^{7-1} \\  & =(0.8)^{7}+7(0.2)(0.8)^{6} \\  & ≈0.5767\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 2) & =1-P(X<2) \\  & ≈1-0.5767 \\  & =0.4233\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places.
